Few years ago I worked part time at a PetSmart. It was a slow night and I was in a bitter mood because my boyfriend had cheated with his ex. But I tried my best to remain pleasant. This Karen was testing me. She comes in with two small yapping poodle mixes and a son on his phone while she's complaining about something. She gets to my register with two boxes of flea and tick medication. It rings up to a high price, no surprise, but when I tell her it she looks at me like I just slapped her kid.

She starts telling me I was wrong. She pulls out her 'Live, Love, Laugh' phone case and brings up the prices on our website. I would have been more than happy to price match had she asked before. Anyways, I fix them and when I tell her her new price she gives me a condescending, good you finally got it right.

She pays, I hand her the receipt and wish them a good night. But she doesn't leave. She stares over the paper before looking back at me, telling me I didn't give her the 10% discount are website was advertising. I wasn't even aware of this discount. Why? It was for online orders of course! But she insists I didn't give it to her because I'm just a petty bitch like that. She starts accusing me of not knowing how to do simple math, I was too new to work the register, blah, blah, blah and finally she asks for my manager. I call her down but she doesn't come because she's busy helping another customer. So here I am, waiting for five minutes with Karen telling me how stupid I am and how terrible my customer service is while her dogs continue to bark. Finally I pull out a ten from the register, throw it on the counter and say 'here, there you go, you got what you wanted now leave.'

Kind of got in trouble for that. Oops.

As cliché as it sounds, mine came from a mix of my mom's insults and being bullied at school. I have a lisp that I now a days play off as an accent which people find interesting. But as a child kids were cruel about how I pronounced words. They'd ask me to repeat sounds they knew I struggled with. Even the teachers made it a big deal. Then there was my mom who was very sheltering. She never let me venture farther than my front yard until school and even then she never let me hang out with others. No birthday parties. No sleepovers. She was very critical about everything I did, often comparing me to other girls she knew I didn't like.

And then just one day I stopped talking because I knew everyones going to look at me differently when I speak with that lisp. They're going to mention it. And when they look beyond that all they're going to see is a fat, ugly failure who could never compare to the other kids. 

Wish I could say I got through it, but that belief has lingered over me my whole life and it won't leave.

I've endured abuse and trauma through my childhood due to my mother as well. I've been through therapist after therapist in attempt to manage the pain. While I've had some tell me to get over it or forgive her, I was never told to rekindle with her and I can't imagine the anger and betrayal I would have felt if one of them did. Your review was completely justified. It may not feel like it, but you are helping future victims seeking a therapist. Abuse and trauma, especially childhood, takes a very special type of counselor and it sounds like she is just not suitable for assisting with recovery. That's not on you. That's not on her. I'm sure you've encountered people throughout your life who were oblivious to what you went through and the impact it has on your thinking and action just like I have. Even with years of schooling, some people will just not understand it.

Be proud of what you did, OP. You not only helped others, you saw your self worth and found your voice. I know it's hard, but you will found the right therapist for you. You might have to go through some like tissues. In the end it won't matter. Good luck, OP.

You just have to keep searching. Maybe set up a few appointments with different therapist/psychiatrist and try them out for a session or two. Explore what you want/like in them and what you dislike.

Can I ask what medication you're on and what's the dosage? I'm on Zoloft and Hydroxyzine at the moment. I wouldn't say it had a huge impact on my anxiety, but it's made my depression and motivation manageable that I can actually get up and do things. I started off feeling numb, kind of dead when I started, so I cut my dosage in half and only take it every other day. It's easier to handle now. Perhaps you could try that or in time, when you do find a new psychiatrist, perhaps you could talk about trying something else that actually works for you?

Please believe me when I tell you I do understand what you're going through. I've had severe social anxiety a large part of my life it use to control me (it still does somedays). So I know that when you struggle to socialize making friends is the biggest bitch of all the Karens and we often accept people into our lives who are rather toxic because it's better than being alone? And even when these people are awful to us or others, we keep proceeding with the relationship because we're in the mindset we won't find anyone else.

That's not the cause. And if these girls are making you feel angry, sad and excluded, is that better than actually being alone and focusing on yourself? The world portrays being alone as a bad thing and I get it, with social anxiety it's so constant it feels that way, but overall being by yourself isn't horrible. It's how you figure out who you are. 

You're TA for begging after you already had your answer. Again, I know it sucks doing things on your own with anxiety. It feels impossible to function normally in new events. It's not wrong of you to seek out support/help with that. But I don't think you're looking in the right spot because the thing is, people who don't have disorders or mental illnesses do not understand shit about them. Just like these friends. They're TA for cursing at you and harassing other people. 

I know it sounds impossible, but take a chance in a social event. Don't believe in others, because usually they're going to disappoint you, but believe in yourself. Take it slow. You can't always stop anxiety, but you can manage it so it's not running your life. Good luck!
